age.evidence: Adult male C57BL/6 J mice (8 weeks old) were purchased from Envigo

sex.evidence: Adult male C57BL/6 J mice (8 weeks old)

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin was dissolved to 0.025 -0.2 mg/mL in saline solution (0.9 % NaCl)... All drugs were administered by intraperitoneal injection.

group_housing.evidence: housed in groups of 6 (cage size: 22 × 22 × 14.5 cm)

day_night_flipped.evidence: housed under standard laboratory conditions on a 12 h light/dark cycle (direction of cycle not specified)

assays.assay_description: HTR individually assessed in an Open Field chamber (43 × 43 × 43 cm), recorded with a camera for 25 min immediately after psilocybin injection; a trained observer counted HTRs between minutes 5–25. Includes dose-response (0.125–3 mg/kg) and antagonist pre-treatments (MDL11939, SB242084, WAY100635).

application_type.evidence: All drugs were administered by intraperitoneal injection.

setup_habituation.evidence: no apparatus habituation described for HTR

setup_restrain.evidence: HTR was individually assessed in an Open Field chamber (43 × 43 × 43 cm)

food_restriction.evidence: food in home cage ad libitum; no food in open-field apparatus during recording

water_restriction.evidence: water in home cage ad libitum; no water in open-field apparatus during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: recorded with a camera device... immediately after psilocybin injection for 25 min

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin induced a dose-dependent inverted-U HTR curve, peaking at 1 mg/kg (~17 HTRs) and decreasing at 3 mg/kg (~9 HTRs). The 5-HT2A antagonist MDL11939 completely blocked HTR; the 5-HT2C antagonist SB242084 (0.1 mg/kg) potentiated HTR at the descending dose (3 mg/kg) but not at 1 mg/kg; the 5-HT1A antagonist WAY100635 had no effect.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin induced a dose-dependent HTR (maximal effect 17.07 ± 1.31 at 1 mg/kg i.p.) that was completely suppressed by the 5HT2AR antagonist MDL11939... Higher doses of psilocybin (3 mg/kg) induced lower HTR (9.00 ± 0.53). The 5HT2CR antagonist SB242084 (0.1 mg/kg) increased HTR exerted by psilocybin (3 mg/kg).

B1_num_measures.evidence: a trained observer counted the number of these responses

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: an initial analysis of HTR throughout time in 5 min-intervals, for 40 min... maximal effect on HTR was reached at the 5-10 min interval

B4_ethological.evidence: head-twitch response is explicitly listed as a non-ethological readout per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: a trained observer counted the number of these responses

E3_bedding.evidence: open fields were thoroughly cleaned with 70 % ethanol — bare floor

D1_continuity.evidence: recorded... immediately after psilocybin injection for 25 min

D2_session_duration.evidence: recorded with a camera device... immediately after psilocybin injection for 25 min

judge_notes: Two assays retained: head-twitch response and rectal body temperature. Dose-response and antagonist pre-treatments collapsed into the relevant single assay per rubric (same paradigm under different pharmacological manipulations).
In vitro radioligand binding assays excluded per rubric (ex vivo/in vitro molecular work).

Temperature D1 set to 'Multiple discrete sessions' (score 1) because the paper reports two distinct timed measurements at -30 min and 0 min plus every 20 min post-drug, all with reported data; one candidate scored 0 but the time-course is clearly multiple measurement timepoints within one day. D2 set to 2 (61 min–6 h) since recording spans 150 min from baseline to final timepoint.
Sex n_male set equal to n_total per assay since all subjects were male; study-level n_male left null as paper does not give a definitive total male count beyond ~302 estimate.
day_night_flipped set to not_reported (high confidence) because paper specifies 12h light/dark cycle but not direction; testing 'in the early morning' is ambiguous regarding cycle direction.
